pathogen: Cotton leaf curl virus (begomovirus complex), spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci
symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaves with thickened veins
Enations (leafy outgrowths) on the underside of veins
Stunted plants with shortened internodes and fewer bolls
Whitefly adults or nymphs visible under leaves

severity_cues.early: Few plants with curled leaves and vein thickening
severity_cues.advanced: Many stunted plants, enations common, boll set badly hit

favorable_conditions: Warm dry weather with high whitefly pressure, weedy hosts, susceptible varieties

treatment.summary: No cure once infected. Kill the vector, rogue the plants, protect the rest
steps: Uproot and destroy infected plants weekly, starting from first symptoms
Control whitefly: spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL at 0.3 ml per litre, rotate with another chemistry to avoid resistance
Keep field borders and weeds clean, they shelter whiteflies
For next season: sow an officially recommended leaf-curl tolerant variety
Avoid excess nitrogen sprays that make lush whitefly-friendly growth

products.name: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL
products.label_source: CIB&RC registered label, waiting period on cotton 15 days

organic: Yellow sticky traps at 10 per acre plus neem oil 1500 ppm at 3 ml per litre
Tolerant varieties and early sowing to escape peak whitefly

source.org: ICAR Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), cotton disease advisory
source.title: Cotton: leaf curl virus and whitefly management

safety_notes: Wear gloves, mask and full sleeves while spraying
Do not pick cotton within 15 days of any insecticide spray
